title: near-miss: assumed logs/basedpyright_report.json is raw basedpyright --outputjson
body: Per-file summary script read data['generalDiagnostics'] and crashed KeyError; the committed lane report is a transformed schema (summary/top_rules/diagnostic_ids rows shaped path:rule:source-line-anchor with #N ordinals). Read the instrument's actual shape before generalDiagnostics-style parsing; raw --outputjson parsing must target the gate's own emitted JSON only.

title: finding: staged proteus_hooks.py repair may be uncounted by committed pool log
body: git status showed index-stage-only modification (M in column 1) of src/CORE/WORMS/expansion/proteus_hooks.py while logs/basedpyright_report.json (committed e7f0608a, recorded 00:10 local) still assigns it 10 reportArgumentType errors. A staged-not-landed fix makes the committed pool log overcount that file; live per-file run confirmed 0E/0W so the repair is complete and lands as slice D with a refreshed report.

title: FALSIFIED: checker-version explanation for whole-tree delta - actual cause is staged prior-lane work
body: First explanation blamed basedpyright 1.40.2 (vs 1.40.1 in docs) for the -45 identity delta. Identity-set diff against HEAD:logs shows the delta is EXACTLY proteus_hooks(-10), aoa_monitor(-11), support_arms(-9), postgres_memory(-15) - work the previous 'continue tasks and land' session applied and staged but never committed, invisible in the partially-read git status. Falsifier: identity math accounts for all 45 without any version effect; rule 'the cited line must be read before accepting an instrument's finding' extended to staging areas - git diff --cached before git status conclusions.

title: near-miss: bash-style env prefix in pwsh evaluated as a command name
body: Wrote 'basedpyright=<path> & basedpyright --version' - bash LABEL=cmd env-prefix syntax does not exist in pwsh; pwsh tried to execute a command named 'basedpyright=' and errored (then the remaining & invocation ran fine, so output was not lost). Use pwsh env syntax ($env:X=) or drop the prefix; harmless here but a real shell-grammar trap when multiplexed into larger command strings.

title: DUAL-ACTOR coordination: Kilo session landing files concurrently in this repo
body: During slice prep, HEAD moved twice under this session: 29005436 (proteus_hooks slice D1) and 81fe5589 (postgres_memory + AOA cluster, 08:10:37) landed by an external session (fits engram 'Kilo Beam finish-up' duty: 'land postgres_memory + AOA cluster'), consuming the staged report refresh this lane staged. learning_pipeline.py modified unstaged at the same time = other actor's in-flight edit. Collision control adopted: my lane touches ONLY the 10 engram-#1557 picks (disjoint set), per-file live recompute after any HEAD move, exclusion of learning_pipeline.py and any file the other actor lands, pathspec-scoped verification before every commit with git restore --staged for foreign files, git commit -- <paths> instead of bare commit, earlier git status conclusion already falsified once (bake item 3) - mid-session staging changes are real, not noise.

title: Report commit would trip DEFAULT_MAX_LINES=150; plan amended to dedicated report commit
body: Reshaping plan said refresh logs/basedpyright_report.json before EVERY pool slice. Measured: one report refresh caries 14+/169- = 183 changed lines versus HEAD (my 118 cleared identities + actor slice-D3 clears), and commit_gate.py:116 blocks any tracked file with added+deleted > 150. Per-commit report inclusion would need ALLOW_BULK_COMMIT on all four slices. Amendment: land picks-only pathspec commits E/F/G/H first, then one dedicated report-only commit with ALLOW_BULK_COMMIT=1 declared and justified. Lesson: check the per-file numstat of an expected artifact BEFORE wiring the commit plan around it.

title: Concurrent index.lock race: commit landed, index write failed; recovery must NOT blind-run git restore --staged
body: Report commit printed: repository has been updated, but unable to write new index file. Commit 710db6e8 still landed (temp index + ref update succeeded; only the final index rewrite lost to the concurrent actor lock holder). Git console advice restore --staged :/ would have unstaged the actor in-flight staged files (learning_grpo, learning_rl, onnx_integration, tensor_utils + their report entry) destroying their workstream. Correct recovery under a dual-actor repo: verify git log -N --stat, diff --cached --name-only for foreign entries, disk space, then leave the index untouched and let the owning actor proceed. 12GB free so disk-full was NOT the cause; a .git/index.lock race is the default hypothesis when a second actor is live.

title: Concurrent actor committed a stale staged report, regressing a derived artifact; corrected via fresh snapshot commit
body: Sequencing: I refreshed the tree report (573E/197W @12:37:18Z) and landed it in 710db6e8. The concurrent actor then landed 6cbb4e65 whose index STILL held their older staged snapshot (692E/233W @12:08:49Z) so HEAD report regressed backward by 183 lines. Lesson: in a dual-actor repo a staged legacy snapshot inside one actor index gets landed by whichever actor commits next; derived artifacts regress instead of monotonic-decrease. Fix is NOT git revert (it would undo their legitimate grpo/rl clears): re-run the checker and commit the fresh snapshot (e5ad798d). Also noted: both lanes independently minted the name pool slice E; slice letters are per-lane variables, not a shared counter.

title: Vendored cp315t builds for tree-sitter language sdists (graphify unblocked)
body: cp315t source builds of tree-sitter language sdists fail four ways, each with a one-step fix: (a) Py_LIMITED_API is set even under Py_GIL_DISABLED in old setups (json 0.24.8) -> binding.c compiles against stable-ABI headers where Py_TYPE/PyModuleDef collapse -> patch setup.py to py_limited_api=False (python 0.25.0 and js 0.25.0 already have the Py_GIL_DISABLED guard; json does not); (b) BdistWheel.get_tag forces cp39/cp310-abi3 wheel tags unconditionally -> pip refuses to install into cp315t envs -> neutralize the forced rename so super().get_tag() emits cp315-cp315t; (c) shipped sdists can be structurally incomplete: python 0.25.0 omits src/scanner.c (parser.c references 5 external_scanner symbols -> LNK2001 x5) and json 0.24.8 omits src/tree_sitter/*.h entirely -> vendor missing files from the upstream grammar repo at the matching tag, NOT from a sibling package: vendoring tree_sitter_python 0.25.0 headers into json broke again because json's parser.c is ABI 15 (TSLanguage.version, ts_field_map_slices) and python 0.25.0 headers are older -> fetch parser.h/alloc.h/array.h from tree-sitter-json v0.24.8; (d) after full bindings, graphify update rebuilt 44636->44645 nodes with built_at_commit==HEAD and the protective refusal condition lifted WITHOUT --force as planned.

title: pip install transactions are all-or-nothing: built is not installed
body: When one wheel in a pip install transaction fails to build, EVERY wheel in that same command is aborted, including ones whose build already succeeded. The 'js built' evidence earlier this lane was wrong: tree_sitter_javascript was not installed at all (ModuleNotFoundError) even though its wheel had compiled. Verify installed state by import, never by 'Successfully built' log lines, and use isolated per-package pip wheel plus individual install when the transaction carries any risk.

title: GLM-10 regression: tracker.generate_quality_report is a module function, not a method
body: GLM 10-pick showed 1 live error at HEAD de3b955c: azazael_cli.py:722 called tracker.generate_quality_report(), but metrics_tracker.py defines generate_quality_report() as a module-level function (line 270) while MetricsTracker only exposes get_report(). Fix: import generate_quality_report and call it directly. Post-fix GLM-10 is 0E/0W live; smoke generate_quality_report() returns benchmark/generated/performance/success_rates keys.
